A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCbiF research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 Sections 6.1–6.3 and Appendix F report original synthetic regression and classification experiments and original MCbiF analysis of previously collected mice data.

after.justification: v2 Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix D retain these original experiments and analyses, adding baseline results and uncertainty estimates.

M1.justification: Both retain the same MCbiF construction from cluster simplices, equivalent nerve construction, Hilbert-function features and average-conflict measures. Additional comparison models and expanded proofs do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic crossing-number regression and order-preservation classification tasks, plus 281 mice observed over nine weeks at nine temporal resolutions. Forward/backward temporal comparisons already appear in v1 Appendix F.3. The added baselines reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Maximum Overlap Distance (MOD) feature baselines to both prediction tasks, and a graph convolutional network (GCN) on Sankey graphs to regression. Tables 1 and 2 confirm their evaluation alongside the retained conditional-entropy and raw-label comparisons, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: The added GCN experiment uses weighted Sankey graphs, three node features and 145 TPE hyperparameter-search trials, introducing a distinct evaluation configuration. Existing regression and classification splits, sample sizes, losses and metrics remain unchanged. Newly stated CNN/MLP training budgets are disclosures, not established changes to earlier settings.

E4.justification: v2 extends correlation and class-separation analyses to ARI and MOD, testing their relationships with crossing numbers and order preservation (Figures 10 and 12). Section 5.3 also examines crossings in optimized mice Sankey layouts. Existing Hilbert-feature comparisons, toy examples and temporal-distance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for regression and classification performance, using 5,000 test-data resamples (Tables 3 and 5). Regression significance testing changes from residual t-tests to Wilcoxon tests. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; it does not establish additional training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline results are added: GCN regression R² is 0.416/0.229 for N=5/10, and ARI/MOD classification accuracy is 0.49/0.46. Raw-label regression scores are revised, including N=5 CNN from -0.006 to 0.267, without an explanation of the cause. Existing MCbiF and CE table scores remain unchanged. Classification HF1 accuracy is 0.97 in both Table 2 versions; v2 corrects v1's prose value of 0.95.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 40 justified nerve equivalence through a brief reference to a prior result. v2 adds Persistent Nerve Lemma 33 and an explicit compatible-cover argument in Proposition 34. It also revises the dimensionality-based advantage condition from M < max|C| - 1 to M < max|C|. Most other mathematical results are retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion broaden claimed empirical superiority from information-based features to baseline features and representation learning. v2 also explicitly foregrounds MCbiF as a complete invariant, whereas v1 described recovery of the partition sequence from its diagonal. The central topological-autocorrelation and non-hierarchy contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the GCN performance gap through MCbiF's higher-order information and connects the mice Sankey crossing to the theoretical crossing bound. It also changes the explanation for restricting analysis to dimensions zero and one from RIVET limitations to simplicity. These refine interpretation and limitations without changing the method.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies batch size 32, 150 epochs and early-stopping patience 10 for CNN/MLP training, alongside detailed GCN inputs, tuning and selected configurations. The reproducibility statement changes the code reference from MCF to MCbiF and explicitly includes experiment-reproduction code. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: Related work expands to ARI and MOD, citing Hubert and Arabie and Peixoto. New references also support GCNs, TPE and Hilbert functions; Lesnick and Wright (2015) is removed. v2 more explicitly contrasts MCbiF's completeness with MCF, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and reorganizes the narrative: background moves to Appendix E, several propositions and remarks move into Appendix B, and experiment definitions move into Appendix D. Existing appendices are reordered, main-text paragraphs are rewritten, and author information and an author-contributions section are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a conference layout, expands comparison tables and adds confidence-interval Tables 3 and 5. Conflict illustrations change from horizontal to vertical arrangements; the theoretical summary and classification boxplots move to appendices. Correlation and classification plots gain baseline panels, and Sankey diagrams are redrawn with optimized layouts.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, bootstrap uncertainty reporting, an expanded equivalence proof and fuller training documentation make the retained research easier to assess. These gains are tempered by new reporting errors: Section 5.1 gives HF1 linear-regression R² as 0.185 where Tables 1 and 3 show 0.448; Table 3 contains a reversed MOD confidence interval; and Appendix D.3 calls τ4 most time-reversible although Figure 14 places the minimum at τ5. The net improvement is therefore limited.
